items.title: Xuanzang
items.context: Tang Buddhist monk, pilgrim and central organiser of translation work.

items.title: Sima Chengzhen
items.context: A figure connecting mountain cultivation, Daoist traditions and Tang court networks.

items.title: Kong Yingda
items.context: Early Tang classical scholar associated with the Correct Meaning of the Five Classics and state learning.

items.title: Heart Sutra
items.context: A concise and influential Buddhist text expressing prajñā and emptiness.

items.title: Daodejing
items.context: A foundational text on Dao, virtue, non-coercive action and naturalness.

items.title: Correct Meaning of the Five Classics
items.context: A major Tang state project in classical commentary and education.

items.title: Analects
items.context: Sayings and encounters associated with Confucius and his disciples, repeatedly reinterpreted by later Confucian traditions.

items.title: Form is not different from emptiness
items.context: A representative line on the relationship between form and emptiness in the Heart Sutra.

items.title: The Dao follows what is naturally so
items.context: Daodejing chapter 25 on humans, earth, heaven, Dao and naturalness.

items.title: Restrain oneself and return to ritual
items.context: Analects 12.1 connects self-regulation, ritual and benevolence.

items.title: Emptiness
items.context: A Buddhist discussion of dependent arising and the absence of fixed self-existence.

items.title: Naturalness
items.context: The Daoist sense of being-so-of-itself, not simply the modern natural world.

items.title: Ritual
items.context: A Confucian concept linking self-cultivation, social order, institutions and classical interpretation.

items.title: Chang'an
items.context: Tang imperial capital and meeting point for politics, education, translation and religious institutions.

items.title: Great Ci'en Monastery
items.context: Buddhist site closely connected with Xuanzang's translation work and the Great Wild Goose Pagoda.

items.title: Louguantai
items.context: An important historical Daoist site on the northern side of Mount Zhongnan.

items.title: Imperial Academy, Chang'an
items.context: A historical gateway into the connection among classics, education and the state.

items.title: Luoyang
items.context: A key city in Sui–Tang political, religious and transport networks.

items.title: Dunhuang
items.context: A major node linking the Central Plains, Central Asian routes and Buddhist visual culture.

items.title: Mount Wutai
items.context: A real mountain region connected with Buddhist pilgrimage and devotion to Mañjuśrī.

items.title: Great Wild Goose Pagoda
items.context: Architectural heritage connected with Xuanzang, textual preservation and Buddhist memory in Chang'an.
